name: AMISA Survey Platform
description: The survey runtime and the source of record for everything a school submits. Questions, validation rules and definitions are stored as data rather than built into screens, so AMISA's own team can change the instrument in the June-to-September window without a vendor release.

name: AMISA Membership Records
description: Who is a member, who enrolled in the data system this year, and the office coordinators AMISA contacts. Enrollment and tuition bands used for peer grouping are read from here.

name: AMISA Data Dictionary
description: The published definition behind every benchmark field — what counts as base salary, what enrollment is measured on, what tuition excludes. Travels with the question at the point of entry, which is where comparability is won.

name: Suppression and Entitlement Rules
description: Minimum peer-group sizes per survey and per office, the permitted grouping axes, and which school may see which office's benchmark. Enforced on every query, including the ones the AI makes.

name: School Spreadsheet Uploads
description: The file path for schools that already keep salary data in a spreadsheet. Columns are mapped once and the same validation runs on every row, so no coordinator retypes what they already have.

name: School Information Systems
description: PowerSchool, Rediker, iSAMS and the spreadsheets smaller schools keep. Shown deliberately unconnected: schools own their data, and a direct read from a school's SIS is a decision for that school, not for the association.

name: Assessment Providers
description: College Board, ACT, IBO, NWEA and Curriculum Associates reports, which arrive at each school rather than at AMISA. Modelled as a future aggregate-only path: student-level detail never leaves the school that owns it, and no assessment values are shown anywhere in this prototype.

name: Audit Log
description: Every consequential action — a sweep applied, a request approved, a summary published — with who did it and when. What makes 'applied by Dereck Rhoads' a record rather than a caption.
